question.prompt:
Figure \(1\) is called a “stack map.” The numbers tell how many cubes are stacked in each position. Fig. \(2\) shows these cubes, and Fig. \(3\) shows the view of the stacked cubes as seen from the front.

Which of the following is the front view for the stack map in Fig. \(4?\)

[Figure 1](figures/1999_AMC_8_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
From the front, stacks directly behind one another appear in the same vertical column. The visible height is the height of the taller stack: a shorter stack cannot hide the part of a taller stack above it.

Read the three front-to-back pairs from left to right. The left pair has heights \(2\) and \(1\), so its front-view height is \(2\). The middle pair has heights \(2\) and \(3\), giving height \(3\). The right pair has heights \(4\) and \(1\), giving height \(4\).

The front view therefore has three adjacent columns of heights \(2,3,4\), increasing from left to right. This is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Keep the taller stack in each column
